text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Former state ministers, members of Chancellor Kohl's CDU party, acquitted of fraud
- Greens leader Joschka Fischer gets worse result than last time but still re-elected as spokesman of parliamentary group
- Steffi Graf's father says tax authorities share responsibility in his tax affair
- High unemployment burdens labour office budget
- Surprising economic growth in second quqrter
- FAZ economic indicator leaps in July
- Still 3.9 million unemployed in August
- Skilled trades fulfil quota of training places
- Deutsche Bank says reputation hit by financial scandal in London
HANDELSBLATT
- German economy recovers in second quarter
- Lufthansa orders McDonnell Douglas freight planes
- Fate of Bremen shipyards hangs in balance
- IG Farben, Nazi-era manufacturer of poison gas, not entitled to return of property in eastern Germany
- Deutsche Bank admits mistakes in Morgan Grenfell affair
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Deutsche Telekom says mobile telephones protected from hackers by secret code
- IG Farben, Nazi-era manufacturer of poison gas, not entitled to return of property in eastern Germany
- Steffi Graf's father attacks tax authorities
- Bonn says German economy has emerged from dip after second quarter rise in growth
- Bundesbank leaves rates unchanged
- Saxony state premier satisified with VW subsidy compromise
- Beef market recovers slightly
DIE WELT
- Economy back on growth path
- Peter Graf feels deceived by tax authorities
- Former state ministers, members of Chancellor Kohl's CDU party, acquitted of fraud
- Foreign Minister Kinkel expects German-Czech declaration soon
- OECD criticises structural and labour cost problems in German economy
- Social Democrats (SPD) put forward list of tax privileges they want to cut
- Morgan Grenfell suspends fund manager
- Retail industry agrees pay deal in Saar state
